parent: AmplifyBio, LLC (venture-backed Battelle spinout; Battelle Memorial Institute reabsorbed it in 2025)
notes: Contract research and manufacturing firm launched by Columbus-based Battelle in 2021 with sites in West Jefferson and New Albany. Its own Form 5500 under EIN 86-2301671 shows 285 retirement plan participants in 2023, JobsOhio's September 2024 report lists 155 jobs retained and 263 committed on a $132.75 million investment, and NBC4 reported more than 200 employees laid off when the company shut down in April 2025. Its own closure notice calls it a startup dependent on investors, so it was not a Battelle subsidiary at the grant date; Battelle took it back in an October 2025 assignment for the benefit of creditors.

The payee is the US holding company of Louis Dreyfus Company, the Dutch-French agricultural trader founded in 1851, which says on its own site that it employs over 20,000 people in more than 100 countries. The project entity in JobsOhio's December 2024 report is Louis Dreyfus Company Upper Sandusky LLC, a $541 million soybean crushing plant in Wyandot County with 114 jobs committed, so the money built the company's own plant.

Columbus ordinance 2574-2025, granting this LLC a ten-year enterprise zone abatement, names the contact as David Pizzotti, principal and co-founder of Trident Capital Group, 15 E. Broad St. Suite 200, Boston MA, matching the payee's Boston address. The grant is a JobsOhio Spec Development (OSIP) award with jobs listed as TBD for a speculative industrial park in east Columbus that Trident is building to lease, so the payee is a developer's project vehicle, not an operating company. No headcount is published for Trident, a small private real-estate firm, so the bucket is inferred.

ELO stands for East Liverpool, Ohio: this is the project entity through which True North, LLC, a West Virginia high-tech business services firm (accounting, payroll, medical billing, collections) with 55 employees, renovated the 31,000 square foot BOSS Building as its own new corporate headquarters. JobsOhio's release names the company, its 55 existing employees and 25 planned additions, so the payee is an operating company building its own building, not a developer.

parent: Unison Risk Advisors (holding company of Oswald Companies and RCM&D)
notes: Employee-owned Cleveland insurance brokerage founded in 1893. Smart Business reports Oswald has about 500 employee-owners across seven Ohio offices plus Michigan and Pennsylvania, and that it is the largest piece of Unison Risk Advisors, the holding company created by its 2020 merger with Baltimore's RCM&D, which has about 1,600 employee-owners in 15 states; Peloton Capital Management took a minority stake in Unison in 2022. Oswald's own Form 5500 shows 900 retirement plan participants in 2023. The JobsOhio release on the downtown Cleveland headquarters move lists 320 jobs retained and 88 committed, and the money paid for the company's own headquarters, so this is a business, not a developer.

parent: Modula S.p.A. (Immobiltec USA Inc is the group's US property-owning affiliate)
notes: Franklin, Ohio's major site plan file for the $24 million Modula expansion at 5000 Commerce Center Drive lists IMMOBILTEC USA, INC. as the owner of that parcel, and the stated purpose is to consolidate Modula's own warehouse and distribution operations into its plant. Modula S.p.A., the Italian maker of automated vertical storage systems, is headquartered in Casalgrande (Reggio Emilia) and says it has three production sites, 14 subsidiaries and over 1,000 employees. Immobiltec is the group's real-estate arm, so the operating company behind the payee is Modula; the exact Immobiltec-to-Modula ownership chain is not published, which is why this is graded C.

Advanced-manufacturing R&D company at 130 E South Street, Barnesville, Ohio, which describes itself on its own site as a small business rooted in eastern Ohio. JobsOhio's October 2024 report shows a $350,000 Revitalization Grant in Belmont County with 3 jobs retained and 15 committed on a $1.0 million investment, so the money went to its own facility. Independent; no parent found.

TPE Acquisition, LLC (Delaware) is listed as a Ryder System subsidiary in Exhibit 21.1 of Ryder's 10-K for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025; it is part of the Whiplash/Port Logistics fulfillment business Ryder bought in 2021, and Whiplash Merchandising, LLC sits beside it on the same list. Ryder's FY2024 10-K reports about 50,700 full-time employees in North America and principal offices in Coral Gables, Florida. JobsOhio's reports show Workforce and Economic Development grants for central Ohio distribution sites with 462 jobs retained by 2026.

parent: Brennan Holdings, LLC (joint venture with Ray Fogg Corporate Properties, LLC)
notes: Ray Fogg Corporate Properties states that it partnered with 'BH (Ohio) Leasing, LLC (an affiliate of Brennan Holdings, LLC)' to develop Seasons Business Park at Route 8 and Seasons Road in Stow, starting with a speculative 108,000 square foot industrial building. JobsOhio's June 2021 report records a Spec Development (OSIP) grant with zero jobs created or retained on a $15.7 million investment, so this is a developer's project vehicle building to lease. Brennan Holdings is the Akron real-estate company of David Brennan; the Longmont, Colorado address on the 990 is a manager's address and the earlier FY2022 filing gave an Akron address, so the Ohio HQ is the better read but is graded C.

Unresolved. An address-named LLC care of a small office suite at 28045 Ranney Parkway, Westlake, Ohio, which took $180,000 of cash in FY2025. No match in JobsOhio's executed-grants reports for 2015 to 2026, no Form 5500 filing, no website, nothing in Google News for the entity or the Westlake address, and the only 'Oberlin Road LLC' in EDGAR full-text search is an unrelated Omega Healthcare Investors subsidiary in Raleigh, North Carolina. Classed as a project vehicle on the strength of the street-address name and the office-suite address alone; if an operating company is behind it the class should be business, so a reviewer should reopen this row.

Independent Dayton contract machining and metal fabrication company. Its own Form 5500 filings under EIN 31-0293030 show 202 retirement plan participants in 2015 and 229 in 2019, and JobsOhio's June 2024 report lists 130 jobs retained and 31 committed on a $1.83 million investment in Montgomery County. No parent company found; no source states where it was founded.

Team sports apparel and equipment company in Holland (Lucas County). Form 5500 for EIN 34-1322656 was filed as Team Sports, Inc. of Holland, Ohio with 89 participants in 2015, and JobsOhio's June 2022 report lists 89 jobs retained and 86 committed on a $1.5 million investment. No parent; despite the name it is a different company from Brennan Industries, Inc. of Solon, which has its own EIN.

Metal fabricator in Kent (Portage County) that filed its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 34-1031850 from Kent, Ohio with 96, 92 and 101 participants in 2015, 2019 and 2023; JobsOhio's August 2024 report lists 80 jobs retained and 20 committed. Participant counts include former employees, so the headcount is right at the 100 line and the bucket is a judgment call. This is a different company from the similarly named ACS Industries of Woonsocket, Rhode Island.

parent: Groupe Lacroix (The Lacroix Group), parent of IML Containers
notes: IML Containers' own history page says it started in 1999 as part of a global expansion by its French corporate parent, The Lacroix Group, a family-owned packaging company founded in 1946; the group's site says it has more than 1,700 employees across 32 sites in 12 countries and lists IML Containers North America as a group site. JobsOhio's November 2023 report records a $100,000 Economic Development Grant for the Alliance (Stark County) plant with 12 jobs retained, 50 committed and $19.09 million invested, so the money built the company's own plant.

parent: Radix Wire & Cable, LLC (Wire Holdings, LLC)
notes: High-temperature wire and cable maker in Euclid, later Glenwillow, Ohio. Form 5500 filings under EIN 46-1783358 were made as Wire Holdings, LLC d/b/a Radix Wire (140 participants in 2015) and later as Radix Wire & Cable, LLC (130 in 2019, 106 in 2023), all from Ohio addresses, so Wire Holdings is the Ohio holding company above the operating business. JobsOhio's July 2021 report lists 76 jobs retained on a $1.4 million investment. No source names an owner above Wire Holdings.

Form 5500-SF filings under EIN 47-5168064 are in the company's own name from Memphis, Tennessee in 2019 and Olive Branch, Mississippi in 2023, with 7 plan participants and business codes for hardware manufacturing and then hardware wholesaling. JobsOhio's November 2024 report records a $75,000 Economic Development Grant for a Lucas County distribution project with 8 jobs retained, 20 committed and $3.26 million invested. No parent company or news coverage was found, and the company is not the similarly named Central Valley Hardware of California, whose history page places it in Northern California since 1939.

parent: AP Shale Logistics ManagementCo LLC, doing business as Tidewater Logistics (Apollo-backed)
notes: FTAI Infrastructure's Q2 2026 10-Q identifies the business as AP Shale Logistics ManagementCo LLC, doing business as Tidewater Logistics, 'a barge and rail transloading company with operations in Ohio, West Virginia and Texas', bought for about $46 million in June 2026, which is after the grant year; the AP in the name and a 2018 Fort Worth Business Press story match Apollo's majority investment. JobsOhio's February 2025 report lists 39 jobs retained and 16 committed in Guernsey and Jefferson counties on a $1.84 million investment. The parent and the Fort Worth headquarters are confirmed, but no source gives a company-wide headcount, so the bucket is a guess from the Ohio figure plus the two other states.

JobsOhio's July 2023 report lists A and A Vending, Inc. in Summit County with a $50,000 Inclusion Grant, 21 jobs retained, 4 committed and a $225,000 investment, matching the Akron address on the 990. The Inclusion Grant, now called the Small Business Grant, is restricted to small businesses and capped at $50,000. No Form 5500 filing exists for the EIN, which also points small.

Maker of overhead and specialty doors in Berlin Heights (Erie County). Its own Form 5500-SF filings under EIN 34-1481994 from Berlin Heights, Ohio show 30, 52 and 67 participants in 2015, 2019 and 2023, and JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists 67 jobs retained and 15 committed on a $1.65 million investment. No parent found.

parent: HBH Holdings, Inc. (owner of Brighton Tru-Edge)
notes: Brighton Tru-Edge, founded in 1914 and operating out of Cincinnati, is North America's largest cold-form tank head maker; its own release names HBH Holdings, Inc. as its parent, and HBH's site gives a Cincinnati headquarters at 4955 Spring Grove Avenue and a portfolio of fabrication, electrical and mechanical contracting companies in Ohio, Tennessee, Kentucky, West Virginia, Mississippi, Louisiana and (from 2025) Germany. JobsOhio's January 2023 report lists 79 jobs retained and 21 committed at the Hamilton County site. HBH publishes no group headcount, so the bucket reflects the Brighton operation and the group total could be higher.

Designs and makes portable lithium iron phosphate battery power systems; its own site gives an address of 11201 Cedar Avenue, Suite 600, Cleveland, Ohio. JobsOhio's July 2024 report records a $50,000 Small Business Grant in Cuyahoga County with zero jobs retained and 7 committed on a $725,000 investment, so it was a startup at the grant date. No Form 5500 filing and no parent found.

JobsOhio's August 2024 report lists HR MACHINE "LLC" in Montgomery County under advanced manufacturing with a $50,000 Small Business Grant, 8 jobs retained, 2 committed and a $505,000 investment, matching the Dayton address on the 990. No Form 5500 filing for the EIN. A machine shop site at hrmachinellc.com turned out to be a different HR Machine with a Pennsylvania phone number, so it is not cited here.

JobsOhio's September 2024 report lists NCF CIM Fabricators, LLC in Richland County under advanced manufacturing with a $50,000 Economic Development Grant, 19 jobs retained, 15 committed and a $3.6 million investment, matching the Mansfield address on the 990. No Form 5500 filing, no website and no news coverage found, so the parent is taken to be the company itself.

Cincinnati risk management and consulting firm. Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 47-4902409 was filed from Cincinnati with 5 participants in 2023, and JobsOhio's November 2020 report records a $50,000 Inclusion Grant in Hamilton County with 1 job retained and 2 committed. The Inclusion Grant is restricted to small businesses.

Columbus technology services company. Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 27-1022200 was filed from Columbus with 12 participants in 2023, and JobsOhio's December 2024 report records a $50,000 Small Business Grant in Franklin County with 6 jobs retained, 4 committed and an $88,730 investment.

JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists this company in Jackson County with a $50,000 Small Business Grant, zero jobs retained, 2 committed and a $100,000 investment, matching the Wellston address on the 990. The Small Business Grant is capped at $50,000 and restricted to small businesses, and the jobs columns hold real numbers rather than the 'TBD' JobsOhio uses for site-development deals, so this reads as an operating small business buying its own equipment rather than a developer; the name does leave room for doubt and no website or news coverage was found. Not the same company as Willis Machinery and Tools of Lucas County, which has its own grant.

JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists UNIQUE REI LLC in Summit County under technology with a $40,000 Small Business Grant, 2 jobs retained, 4 committed and a $7,000 investment, matching the Stow address on the 990. JobsOhio's own industry tag and the tiny fixed-asset figure point to an operating services company, not a real-estate vehicle, although the REI in the name invites the other reading. No Form 5500 filing, and uniquerei.com is a parked domain.

Electrical contractor in Cleveland. JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists a $40,000 Small Business Grant in Cuyahoga County with 16 jobs retained, 5 committed and a $28,544 investment; FY2025 cash paid was $27,116. No Form 5500 filing for the EIN, which also points small. No parent found.

Financial services firm in Kent (Portage County). Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 83-1436259 was filed from Kent, Ohio with 2 participants in 2023, and JobsOhio's November 2023 report records a $25,000 Inclusion Grant with 2 jobs retained, 3 committed and a $13,000 investment. The Inclusion Grant is restricted to small businesses.

Form 5500-SF filings under EIN 46-1250974 are in the company's own name from Wilmot, Ohio in 2019 (4 participants) and Wooster, Ohio in 2023 (9 participants), with the business code for home furnishing wholesalers, matching the Wooster address on the 990. The $25,000 paid in FY2025 is the Small Business Grant amount. No match in JobsOhio's executed-grants reports and no news coverage, so the parent is taken to be the company itself.

Excavating contractor in Crestline (Crawford County). Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 84-2637427 was filed from Crestline, Ohio with 1 participant in 2023 under the heavy construction business code, and JobsOhio's April 2024 report records a $25,000 Small Business Grant with 20 jobs retained, 2 committed and a $120,000 investment. It sells excavation services, so the money went to its own equipment, not to developing property for others.

Design-build firm in Toledo. Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 45-4317719 was filed from Toledo, Ohio with 6 participants in 2019 and 4 in 2023 under the specialized design services business code, and JobsOhio's December 2023 report records a $25,000 Inclusion Grant in Lucas County under advanced manufacturing with 2 jobs retained, 1 committed and a $460,000 investment. It sells design and construction services, so it is a business, not a developer holding real estate for others.

Metal finishing shop in Cincinnati. JobsOhio's May 2024 report lists it in Hamilton County under advanced manufacturing with a $25,000 Small Business Grant, 24 jobs retained, 5 committed and a $90,000 investment. No Form 5500 filing for the EIN, and mechanicalfinishers.com is a parked domain, so the company's own site could not be used.

Concrete contractor in Tallmadge (Portage County). Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 31-1506957 was filed from Tallmadge, Ohio with 6 participants in 2023, and JobsOhio's July 2024 report records a $25,000 Small Business Grant with 30 jobs retained and 10 committed. A contractor selling concrete work is an operating business, not a real-estate developer.

Unresolved beyond size. The $25,000 paid in FY2025 is the JobsOhio Small Business Grant amount, which is capped at $50,000 and restricted to small businesses, and the EIN prefix 99 shows the company was registered in 2023 or later. No match in JobsOhio's executed-grants reports for 2015 to 2026, no Form 5500 filing, nothing in EDGAR full-text search and nothing in Google News for the name. Classed as a business from the grant program and the Dayton street address; the parent is taken to be the company itself for want of any source.

Machine shop in Kent (Portage County). Its own Form 5500-SF under EIN 34-1638249 was filed from Kent, Ohio with 4 participants in 2023, and JobsOhio's January 2024 report records a $25,000 Inclusion Grant under advanced manufacturing with 4 jobs retained, 1 committed and a $65,000 investment.

FDIC records for certificate 59292 show Adelphi Bank was established on 18 January 2023 in Columbus, Ohio, runs one office, and reported 24 employees and $87.6 million of assets in its 30 June 2025 call report. It is Ohio's only minority depository institution and the first new Black-owned bank in the United States since 2000; JobsOhio committed $150,000 through its Small Business Grant program and paid $24,291 in FY2025. An independent, for-profit chartered bank, so it is classed as a business, not a nonprofit.

Awning maker in Canton (Stark County). JobsOhio's November 2024 report records a $20,000 Small Business Grant under advanced manufacturing with 2 jobs retained, 1 committed and a $25,560 investment. No Form 5500 filing for the EIN, which also points small.

Despite the name this is a trucking and delivery business: its own Form 5500 under EIN 86-3744676 was filed from New Concord, Ohio with 3 participants in 2023 under the couriers and express delivery business code, and JobsOhio's December 2024 report lists it in Franklin County under logistics and distribution with a $25,000 Small Business Grant, 4 jobs retained, 2 committed and a $5,000 investment. FY2025 cash paid was $10,400.
